issues.description: Class name and top-level structure mismatch: the problem statement UML and the reference solution expect a public class named 'Farm' (used as the main class representing the farm), but the template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares a different public class name 'AnimalFarm' and contains duplicated/nested package and class declarations (malformed code). This inconsistency (1) prevents students from mapping the specification to the starter code and (2) causes compilation errors because the file contains nested/duplicated package and class declarations instead of a single well-formed public class 'Farm'.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the malformed template file with a single public class named 'Farm' that matches the problem UML and the reference solution. Concretely: (1) ensure the file declares 'package de.tum.cit.ase;' only once; (2) declare 'public class Farm { ... }' as the top-level public class (matching the filename Farm.java); (3) remove duplicate/nested package or class declarations that appear in the current template; and (4) provide the expected Farm API (a private List<Animal> animals initialized in a no-arg constructor, getter/setter for animals, addAnimal(Animal), feedAllAnimals(), and singFarmSong() with an appropriate private helper singFarmSongVerse(Animal)). Keep method bodies pedagogical (students can complete behavior where intended), but the class and file must compile and present the expected Farm identifier and structure.
